mechanism: Vitamin E at high doses (>400 IU daily) may potentiate anticoagulant effects and increase bleeding risk, while deutetrabenazine has no direct anticoagulant properties but concurrent use warrants monitoring.
action: Monitor patients taking both agents for signs of bleeding; vitamin E supplementation should generally remain below 400 IU daily if concurrent anticoagulation therapy is present, though deutetrabenazine alone does not require dose adjustment.
